newsitem.title: USA: Iowa corn planting starts, oats plantings advance.
newsitem.headline: Iowa corn planting starts, oats plantings advance.

text.p: Iowa farmers planted corn despite cool weather during the week ended Sunday, and four percent of the acreage was planted versus none the previous week, according to Iowa's Agriculture Statistics Service.
A year ago 20 percent of corn acreage was planted and the five-year average was 15 percent.
Oat planting advanced to 81 percent versus 86 a year ago and the 73 average. Oats had emerged on 15 percent of the acreage, versus 21 a year ago and the 33 average.

Wet fields impeded planting in the southwest and south central areas of the state. Despite gains in fertilizer application, seedbed preparation and seedings, soil temperatures across the state still have been reported as being too cool for proper corn germination.
Generally, temperatures were below normal throughout the week before climbing to near seasonal readings Saturday and a little above normal on Sunday.
Topsoil moisture was rated 21 percent surplus, 76 adequate and three short. Subsoil moisture was rated 15 percent surplus, 81 adequate and four short.
